'''Mark H. Holmes''' is an American applied mathematician and Professor of Mathematics at [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]], where he served as Chair of the Department of Mathematical Sciences, and was the founding Director of the Center for Modeling, Optimization and Computational Analysis (MOCA).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://moca.rpi.edu|title=MOCA |date= |access-date=2019-12-16}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mark H. Holmes was born in [[Onawa, Iowa]] on November 7, 1950. He attended [[Colorado State University]], where he earned his B.S. in 1973, and the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], where he received his PhD in mathematics in 1978. His PhD thesis advisor was [[Julian Cole]].

==Research==
He is known for his contributions in mathematical biology, including mechanoreception (hearing<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eaton.math.rpi.edu/Articles/forbes.12.3.1984.v2.png  | title=Beyond Hearing Aids |publisher=Forbes, December 3, 1984 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://eaton.math.rpi.edu/Articles/sci_news.5.17.1986.pdf  | title=Catching a vivid earful of sound | publisher= Science News, May 17, 1986}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://eaton.math.rpi.edu/Articles/sci_news.5.7.1988.pdf  | title=Sounds in the unwrapped inner ear | publisher=Science News, May 7, 1988 }}</ref> and touch<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eaton.math.rpi.edu/Articles/Gazette.10.9.1994.pdf | title=Sun on skin, a cat's rub defined by formula | publisher=The Sunday Schenectady Gazette, October 9, 1994 }}</ref>), neurobiology (Parkinson's Disease and the sleep-wake cycle<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rpi.edu/dept/science/news/newsletters/2010/March2010.pdf|title=The Mathematics Behind a Good Night's Sleep |publisher=Rensselaer School of Science Newsletter, March 2010 }}</ref>), and tissue mechanics (articular cartilage).

==Educational initiatives==
He has been instrumental in numerous educational initiatives.  This has included starting the Rensselaer laptop program (in 1995), co-directing Project Links for developing web-based learning modules (1995–2003),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rpi.edu/dept/NewsComm/Campus_News/jan00/jan_29/home.html|title=Project Links Receives Award for Excellence |publisher=Rensselaer Campus News, January 29, 2001 }}</ref> creating the Gateway Exam (1999–2007),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eaton.math.rpi.edu/Articles/gateway_exam_talk_2002.pdf |title=On-line assessment using a gateway exam |publisher=Presentation at Colloquium on Teaching and Learning, Rensselaer, May 2002 }}</ref> organizing the Rensselaer Calculus Video Project (2000–2008), and heading the Rensselaer GAANN program (2009–2016) for recruiting, and retaining, under-represented groups in mathematics.  Holmes has written several textbooks based on some of the applied math courses offered at Rensselaer.{{cn|date=April 2025}}

==Honors and awards==
*[[Guggenheim Fellow]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/mark-h-holmes/ |title=Mark H. Holmes |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation }}</ref>
*[[Y.C. Fung]] Young Investigator Award<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/achievement-awards/y-c-fung-young-investigator-award|title=Y.C. Fung Young Investigator Award Recipients |publisher=The American Society of Mechanical Engineers |date= }}</ref>
*Premier Award for Excellence in Engineering Education Courseware<ref>{{cite web|url=https://premieraward.org/premier-courseware-of-2000/|title=Premier Courseware of 2000 |publisher=Synthesis and SUCCEED Engineering Education Coalitions }}</ref>
*American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Curriculum Innovation Award for 2001

==Books==
*''Introduction to Differential Equations'', XanEdu Publishing, 2020.
*''Introduction to the Foundations of Applied Mathematics (2nd Ed)'', [[Springer International Publishing]], 2019.
*''Introduction to Scientific Computing and Data Analysis'', Springer, 2016.
*''Introduction to Perturbation Methods (2nd Ed)'', Springer, 2013.
*''Introduction to Numerical Methods in Differential Equations'', Springer, 2007.
